svg.text: Sociology optional — toolkit first, India next, craft always
the deepest GS overlap of any optional: GS-1 society · GS-2 welfare · essay · interview
PAPER 1 — THE TOOLKIT
Sociology as science · methods (survey, fieldwork, comparative)
THINKERS — Marx: class, alienation · Durkheim: facts, suicide
Weber: action, bureaucracy, Protestant ethic · Parsons: systems
Merton: anomie, functions · Mead: self (I–Me)
Structures: stratification (caste-class debate) · work · religion
Kinship & family types · social change lines
Development & dependency · movements · population · urban
formula: thinker → concept → application → critique
PAPER 2 — INDIAN SOCIETY
Lenses: indological · structural-functional · Marxist
Colonial impact · village canon: Srinivas · Beteille · Dube
Caste (features, theories, change) · class · tribe continuum
Kinship regions · religious communities
Change: sanskritization · westernization · modernization (Y. Singh)
Movements: peasant · Dalit/backward · women · environment
Challenges: communalism · regionalism · migration · informality
rule: one Indian study + one datum per answer — or it is an essay, not sociology
TWELVE-WEEK FIRST PASS
wk 1-2 science+methods · wk 3-5 thinkers (two/week + passages) · wk 6-7 stratification/kinship/religion · wk 8-10 paper-2 + ethnography notebook · wk 11 movements + current · wk 12 PYQ map
big pool warning: margins come from craft (names, studies, data) — not syllabus completion
